items.title: [pympp] pympp allows excessive sponsored transaction fees through padded calldata
items.summary: DetailsWhen the server acts as the fee_payer, pympp 0.8.0 validates calldata using eth_abi decoding, which is lenient about trailing bytes. The FeePayerPolicy caps gas_limit (≤ 2 M) and max_fee_per_gas (≤ 100 Gwei) but does not check calldata length.Tempo uses legacy calldata gas pricing: 16 gas per non-zero byte. Appending N bytes of 0x01 padding inflates actual gas used by N × 16 while keeping gas_limit and max_fee_per_gas within policy caps. The server cosigns and broadcasts the padded transaction, draining its fee-payer wallet.Vulnerable code path: FeePayerPolicy in fee_payer_policy.py (pympp 0.8.0) enforces maxGas = 2_000_000 and maxFeePerGas = 100 Gwei but has no calldata.length bound. The policy check passes because the inflated gas comes from intrinsic calldata cost, not the declared gas_limit.Note: In our experiment, we enforce an 16 KB max_header_length, which caps the maximum effective padding at roughly 5,500 bytes. The default padding in this PoC (5,500 bytes) is within that limit.PoCThe PoC is provided below. It is configured to reproduce the attack on Tempo Moderate testnet within a Docker environment. Download the PoC and run:unzip pympp_python_PoC.zipcd pympp_pythondocker build -t pympp-padding .docker run --rm pympp-paddingThere are more details in pympp_python/README.mdImpactIn our experiment, a malicious client can force the server to pay ~5x the normal transaction fee. This dramatically increases operational costs and completely destroys the profit margin on low-cost items.Please provide a way to share the PoC in .zip format to you. Thank you!Referenceshttps://github.com/tempoxyz/pympp/security/advisories/GHSA-v858-xh7w-8jr5https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-63634https://github.com/tempoxyz/pympp/commit/57a750d0d980b8e6c3bea62a40b7621f176ff1f0https://github.com/tempoxyz/pympp/releases/tag/v0.9.1https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-v858-xh7w-8jr5

items.title: [arize-phoenix] Phoenix: Format String Injection in applyChatTemplate
items.summary: SummaryA format string injection vulnerability in the applyChatTemplate GraphQL endpoint allows an attacker to read server-side environment variables, cryptographic secrets, and internal module attributes directly from the API response. On default Phoenix installations where authentication is disabled the endpoint is reachable with no credentials. On auth-enabled deployments, any account regardless of privilege level is sufficient to exploit it.ImpactServer filesystem paths, loaded Python module names, and internal configuration constants are fully disclosed, an attacker with network access can read the full server os.environ including the admin credentials hardcoded in phoenix.auth.Successful exploitation allows an attacker to extract PHOENIX_SECRET, the master key used to sign all JWTs and derive the Fernet encryption key protecting stored credentials (LLM API keys, OAuth tokens). With this key, an attacker can forge admin-level session tokens and decrypt all secrets stored in the database.Affected VersionsFirst vulnerable release: arize-phoenix-v13.0.0 (2026-02-13)Latest confirmed vulnerable release: arize-phoenix-v14.8.0 (2026-04-17)Affected Component applyChatTemplate GraphQL query endpoint (src/phoenix/server/api/queries.py:1638) FStringTemplateFormatter._format() template rendering function (src/phoenix/utilities/template_formatters.py:272) DotDict.__getattr__() ineffective attribute access control (src/phoenix/utilities/template_formatters.py:90)Proof of Conceptpayload as txt with an image performing the exploit below.Payload:{  "query": "query($t: PromptChatTemplateInput!, $o: PromptTemplateOptions!) { applyChatTemplate(template: $t, templateOptions: $o) { messages { content { ... on TextContentPart { text { text } } } } } }",  "variables": {    "t": { "messages": [{ "role": "USER", "content": [{ "text": { "text": "{u.__class__.__bases__[0].__init__.__globals__[_os].environ}" } }] }] },    "o": { "format": "F_STRING", "variables": { "u": { "x": 1 } } }  }}Suggested FixThree mitigations are recommended in combination: restrict attribute traversal at the Formatter.get_field() level (not the wrapper class), add IsAuthenticated permission to the applyChatTemplate resolver, and limit F_STRING format to trusted system-defined templates only.Best Regards,OmarReferenceshttps://github.com/Arize-ai/phoenix/security/advisories/GHSA-gfv3-m769-5xm3https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-53998https://github.com/Arize-ai/phoenix/pull/13197https://github.com/Arize-ai/phoenix/commit/e7224a685589f2ffae1fefcc68ff210bd6ad28b8https://github.com/Arize-ai/phoenix/releases/tag/arize-phoenix-v15.7.0https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-gfv3-m769-5xm3
